definitions.explanation: The initial teaching or introduction to a skill, art, or discipline. Implies personal, hands-on guidance from someone experienced.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}に{将棋|しょうぎ}の{手|て}ほどきを{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I received my first lessons in shogi from my father.

examples.japanese: {茶道|さどう}の{手|て}ほどきをしてもらった。
examples.english: I was given an introduction to the tea ceremony.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}から{料理|りょうり}の{手|て}ほどきを{受|う}けたのが{今|いま}の{仕事|しごと}につながった。
examples.english: The cooking lessons I received from my grandmother led to my current career.

notes:
USAGE:
Implies personal, one-on-one guidance rather than classroom instruction. Often used for traditional arts and skills. The most common patterns are {手|て}ほどきを{受|う}ける (to receive instruction) and {手|て}ほどきをする (to give instruction).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手|て}ほどきを{受|う}ける (to receive initial instruction)
- {手|て}ほどきをする (to give initial instruction)
- 〜の{手|て}ほどき (introduction to ~)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {入門|にゅうもん}: introduction to a field (more formal, can be self-study)
- {指導|しどう}: guidance, coaching (broader, ongoing instruction)
